title: Battery & power
blurb: Not charging, draining fast, sleep and wake problems.

remedies.title: Check my laptop battery's health
remedies.why: Batteries lose capacity over time; the system can report how much is left.

steps.text: Run DeskMedic's Health check: it reads the battery's design vs. full-charge capacity.
In Terminal (cmd) run powercfg /batteryreport for a detailed history.
System Settings › Battery › Battery Health (ⓘ); System Information › Power shows the cycle count.
Below ~80% of the original capacity, a battery replacement is worth considering.

remedies.title: Add Hibernate to the power menu
remedies.why: Hibernate saves everything to disk and uses no battery, unlike Sleep.

steps.text: Power options › Choose what the power buttons do › Change settings that are currently unavailable › tick Hibernate.

remedies.title: Charger gets hot, whines or the plug sparks
remedies.why: Warm is normal; very hot, burning smells, sparks or damaged cables are not.

steps.text: Unplug a charger that smells, sparks or has a damaged cable, and stop using it.
Use the maker's charger or a certified replacement of the right wattage.
Keep chargers in open air, not under blankets.

remedies.escalate: Ask IT for a replacement charger for work laptops.

remedies.title: Battery stops charging at 80%
remedies.why: Battery care features hold the charge at 80% to make the battery last longer.

steps.text: This is usually on purpose. Mac: Battery › ⓘ next to Battery Health › Optimized Battery Charging.
Windows laptops: the maker's app (Lenovo Vantage, MyASUS, Dell Power Manager, HP) or Settings › Power & battery › Smart charging.
Turn it off before a trip if you need the full charge.
